topic: Peas are a gut-health MVP: they bring fiber that helps keep digestion moving, plus prebiotic fibers that feed your beneficial gut bacteria. They also contain resistant starch and fermentable carbs that can support a healthier microbiome. And here’s what makes them even more valuable—those fermentable fibers get broken down by your gut microbes into short-chain fatty acids like butyrate, which help nourish your gut lining, reduce inflammation, and support overall gut function. On top of that, peas provide plant-based protein and polyphenols that further support microbial diversity and metabolic health. #plantbased #healthyfood #easyrecipes #fiber

topic: If your poop feels sharp, you could have something called an anal fissure — which is a small cut in your anal canal — or possibly a painful hemorrhoid. And when that happens, the goal is simple: You need to make your poop softer, smoother, and easier to pass. That usually means treating constipation, and increasing both types of fiber: Soluble fiber pulls water into the stool and helps create a softer, gel-like poop that is easier to pass. Good examples include oats, chia seeds, psyllium husk, beans, lentils, apples, and berries. Insoluble fiber adds bulk and helps move stool through the gut more efficiently. You’ll find it in vegetables, whole grains, bran, nuts, seeds, and leafy greens. If your stool is hard, dry, or painful, pushing harder can make hemorrhoids worse and keep an anal fissure from healing. So if you’re dealing with sharp poop pain, don’t ignore it. Start by softening the stool, increasing fiber slowly, drinking enough water, and get checked if there’s bleeding, severe pain, or symptoms that don’t improve. Save this if you struggle with constipation, hemorrhoids, or painful poop. #poop #constipation #fiber #hemorrhoids
